ImageDescription.value: Leonardo da Vinci, The Virgin and Child with Saint Anne, oil on panel, begun about 1503 and left unfinished at his death in 1519. The Virgin sits on her mother's lap and leans towards the Child, who holds a lamb, the animal of sacrifice, so that three generations and the destiny of the fourth figure are held in a single pyramid. Louvre, Paris.

ImageDescription.value: Fresco of Jesus the Virgin Mary and Joseph in the Chapel of the Immaculate Conception by Marcus Dubois. The Basilica of Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré is a basilica set along the Saint Lawrence River in Quebec, Canada, 30 kilometres (19 mi) east of Quebec City, and one of the five national shrines of Canada. It has been credited by the Catholic Church with many miracles of curing the sick and disabled. It is an important Catholic sanctuary, which receives about a half-million pilgrims each year. Since 1933 they have included members of the Anna Fusco Pilgrimage from Connecticut, United States of America. The peak period of pilgrimage is around July 26, the feast of Saint Anne, the patron saint of sailors.

Artist.value: Wilfredor
